<ticket source="">
# # Filtering by `done=false` shows the completed tasks

- Ticket: request
- State: open

## Description

# Filtering by `done=false` shows the completed tasks

**Type:** bug

On the page, choosing "Show: Open" lists the tasks that are done, and hides the open ones. The API does the same:

1. Create two tasks, mark one of them done.
2. `GET /api/tasks?done=false`
3. Expected: only the open task. Actual: only the done one.

`?done=true` looks right.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `GET /api/tasks?done=false` returns only the tasks that are not done.
2. `GET /api/tasks?done=true` returns only the done tasks; without `done`, every task is listed as before.
3. Any other value of `done` (for example `?done=yes` or `?done=`) answers `400` with `{"error": "done must be true or false"}`.
4. A test reproduces the bug and passes with the fix.
</ticket>

plan.summary:
Bug: `GET /api/tasks?done=false` returns done tasks. Cause: `src/app.ts` passes the raw query string to `listTasks`, and `src/tasks.ts` tests `filter.done ? 1 : 0` on it. The string "false" is truthy, so it selects done tasks. `?done=true` only works by accident.

The fix is one small task for the back role, with no design, UX or QA task. The page needs no change. `public/app.js` already sends `?done=false`, `?done=true` or no parameter, so it is fixed once the API is.

The task has three parts:
1. In `src/app.ts`, the GET `/api/tasks` handler reads `url.searchParams.get("done")`. Null means the parameter is absent and every task is listed. Exactly "true" or "false" becomes a boolean. Anything else answers 400 with `{"error": "done must be true or false"}`. That includes the empty string (`?done=`), `yes` and `TRUE`, which are rejected. A repeated `done` parameter uses the first value.
2. `listTasks` in `src/tasks.ts` takes `filter: { done?: boolean }` and keeps the existing SQL, which passes `done ? 1 : 0`. Nothing else calls `listTasks` with a string.
3. In `test/tasks.test.ts`, regression tests go through the HTTP API with one done and one open task. The shared server and in-memory database persist across tests, so the tests must check that the specific created ids are present or absent, not exact list contents. They cover `done=false`, `done=true`, no filter, and the 400 cases (`yes`, empty, `TRUE`). The `done=false` test must fail on the old code.

The package has no lint or typecheck script. The check is `npm test`.

No questions block the work. The triage step already settled the edge-case rule (exact `true`/`false`, else 400).

tasks.goal: Fix the done filter of GET /api/tasks. (1) In src/app.ts, in the GET branch of `/api/tasks`, read `url.searchParams.get("done")`: null (absent) -> list all tasks; exactly "true" -> true; exactly "false" -> false; any other value, including the empty string (`?done=`, which must NOT be treated as absent), `yes` and `TRUE` -> `send(res, 400, { error: "done must be true or false" })`. A repeated `done` parameter: the first value is used. (2) In src/tasks.ts change `listTasks(db, filter: { done?: boolean } = {})`: keep `undefined` -> all tasks, otherwise `WHERE done = ?` with `filter.done ? 1 : 0` on a real boolean. Contract: the string-to-boolean parsing and validation live only in src/app.ts; listTasks takes a boolean. (3) In test/tasks.test.ts add regression tests through the HTTP API with the existing `call` helper and the shared server (state persists across tests, so create tasks, mark one done via PATCH, and assert that the created ids are present or absent rather than the exact list): `?done=false` returns the open task and not the done one (this test must fail on the old code); `?done=true` returns the done one and not the open one; no filter returns both; `?done=yes`, `?done=` and `?done=TRUE` answer 400 with body `{ error: "done must be true or false" }`. Do not touch public/. Run `npm test` (the only check; the project has no lint or typecheck script) and make sure it passes.

reviews.summary:
No problems found. I read the whole diff (src/app.ts, src/tasks.ts, test/tasks.test.ts) and ran `npm test` myself: 13 of 13 pass. I did not re-run the tests against the old code. I accepted the implementer's claim that the done=false and 400 tests fail there, because the old code plainly passed the raw string, so "false" was truthy.

AC1 and AC2: `done` is read with `searchParams.get`. Absent (null) lists all tasks. Exactly "true" or "false" becomes a real boolean, and `listTasks` filters with `done = ?` on 1 or 0. A repeated parameter uses the first value, which is how `get` behaves. The `listTasks` signature change is type-consistent. `src/app.ts` is the only caller, and parsing lives only there, as the plan required.

AC3: `yes`, an empty value (`?done=`) and `TRUE` all answer 400 with `{error: "done must be true or false"}`. The null check keeps the empty string from being treated as absent. The 400 tests assert both the status and the exact body.

AC4: the regression tests go through the real HTTP API with the existing `call` helper. They create an open task and a done task, mark one done by PATCH, and check that the created ids are present or absent. They do not depend on the exact list, so the shared server and database state is fine. The done=false test would fail on the old code, so it reproduces the bug. The done=true and no-filter tests also pass on the old code, but they guard AC2 against regression, so they are acceptable.

Scope: `public/` was not touched, and nothing else changed. The project has no lint or typecheck script, so none was run. I did not run the page in a browser. I did not run a separate security review, but the change only narrows accepted query input, and the value reaches SQL only as a bound 0 or 1.

report.summary:
No vulnerabilities confirmed. I read the full diff (src/app.ts, src/tasks.ts, test/tasks.test.ts) against main. I did not run the tests or the server.

The change narrows input. In GET /api/tasks, `done` is read once with `searchParams.get`. Only absent, exactly "true" or exactly "false" pass. Anything else, including the empty string, gets a fixed 400 body. The body is a constant string, so no user input is reflected and nothing leaks.

`listTasks` now takes a real boolean, and SQL uses a bound parameter (`done = ?` with 1 or 0). The query string never reaches the SQL text, so there is no injection path. Before the change the raw string went into `filter.done ? 1 : 0`, which was a logic bug (wrong data returned) but not an injection.

Validation fails closed: an invalid value is rejected before any database read. No new dependencies, no package.json change, no secrets, no logging added. package.json has no dependencies at all, so an audit has no target.

Checked: injection into SQL, validation bypass (empty value, repeated parameter, case variants, which all get a 400 or use the first value), error behaviour, new dependencies, secrets. A repeated `done` parameter uses the first value; that affects only the caller's own filter, not what they can access.

Not checked: the rest of the app, authentication and authorization (the app appears to have none, and the diff touches none), the front end in public/, and runtime behaviour. Unconfirmed candidates: none.
